clues.text: This tiny town has a flat heart, ringed by hills and hard rock. It sits in the north mid part of a green hill state.
clues.narrowing: Points to a tiny city in a flat pocket ringed by hills in a mountain state.

source.quote: The city center is a flat clay zone (elevation 520 ft; 160 m), surrounded by hills and granite ledges.

clues.text: Winters here are long, cold, and snowy, with snow staying on the ground for long stretches. Summers are warm and humid.
clues.narrowing: Keeps mountain-state capitals with long, snowy winters.

source.quote: Montpelier features a humid continental climate (Köppen Dfb), with long, cold, and snowy winters, short springs and autumns, and warm, humid summers.

clues.text: This town was selected as the state capital in 1805. Its own citizens donated money to build the first state house.
clues.narrowing: Cuts the list to the town selected as capital in 1805, whose citizens funded the state house.

source.quote: Montpelier was selected as state capital in 1805, and citizens of the town donated funds to build the first state house.

clues.text: This is the least populous state capital in the United States. It is so small that it has no McDonald's restaurant at all.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: only one capital is the nation's least populous.

source.quote: The site of Vermont's state government, it is the least populous state capital in the United States.

clues.text: The governor of Vermont works in this tiny city. Lawmakers meet in its state house, a short walk from the river.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: the governor and lawmakers of Vermont work in this city.

source.quote: is the capital city of the U.S. state of Vermont

reveal.blurb: Picked as the capital in 1805 for its spot near the center of the state, this little river town has fewer people than any other state capital. Its gold-domed state house faces the river, and red hearts cover its shop windows every Valentine's Day. Montpelier is the capital of Vermont.
